status: Primary issuer review complete; one research JSON; no model changes.
decisive_findings: AT&S explicitly identified Marvell on September 22 as the previously unnamed customer in its June Kulim expansion announcement. The announced customer pair is AMD and Marvell. It must not be attributed to Intel.
Ibiden’s new October 29 investment is principally a later capacity addition: H2 FY2029 ramp, or October 2029–March 2030. It does not add capacity in calendar 2027 or 2028.

The separate existing Ibiden EMIB-T ramp remains scheduled for H2 FY2027, or October 2027–March 2028. Existing-plant support for earlier demand is possible, with no disclosed Intel-specific volume allocation.

Customer funding is substantively supported, but it finances supplier investment and obligations. Neither customer advance liabilities nor project/service payments justify recurring free cash without matching delivery, capital and pricing economics.

ibiden.fiscal_mapping: Ibiden FY2026 is April 1, 2026–March 31, 2027. FY2027 is April 2027–March 2028; FY2028 is April 2028–March 2029; FY2029 is April 2029–March 2030; FY2030 is April 2030–March 2031.

investment_notice.facts: Approximately JPY151B, principally Gama Cell6 and an overseas plant, for high-performance IC package substrates. Notice describes CPUs and sequential operation from FY2029. No customer name or unit allocation is disclosed.

presentation.locator: Slide 13, Capital Expenditure for the growth of the electronics business; visually inspected
presentation.facts: Cell6 shows prior JPY220B plus newly added JPY150B, with the product label AI ASIC and operations from FY2029. Cell8 separately shows prior JPY280B for AI GPU substrates, operations from FY2027. Cell7/Cell9 terms and decisions remain targeted for completion within FY2026.
presentation.scope_control: Do not add the original JPY220B and JPY280B to the original JPY500B plan again. The JPY150B presentation figure rounds the JPY151B notice. The table does not mean every earlier Cell6 activity is postponed to FY2029.

latest_qa.locator: PDF pages 3–5, Questioners 1–5; October 30 event posted November 2
latest_qa.facts: New investment ramps H2 FY2029 and contributes from FY2030, outside existing FY2030 financial targets. Management calls this investment EMIB rather than EMIB-T. It says the EMIB-T H2-next-fiscal-year mass-production schedule is unchanged. New buildings require at least four years from investment decision; management expects substrate demand to exceed industry capacity.
latest_qa.scope_control: Notice says CPU, presentation says AI ASIC, and Q&A says EMIB. Preserve the differing descriptions; these sources do not establish an Intel CPU-only allocation or quantified Intel packaging output. Supplier demand forecasts are management judgments, not measured Intel revenue.

earlier_qa.may_facts: Management says customers will bear investment costs under agreements and a portion will be paid in advance; no additional financing planned then. Human-resource and lead-time constraints limit expansion beyond the original plan through FY2028.
earlier_qa.august_facts: EMIB-T technical establishment was mostly complete and moving into yield improvement. Gama sequential operation was expected at FY2027 end, with FY2028 performance contribution; existing plants could address earlier demand. This supports a phased ramp rather than requiring zero deliveries until a new building reaches scale.

observed_funding.locator: PDF pages 5 and 9, current liabilities and operating cash flow; visually inspected
observed_funding.interpretation: The advance increase is observable cash-flow support and sits within current liabilities. It is not permanent operating profit or evidence that Intel paid this entire amount. Customer-specific settlement, refund, amortization and allocation terms are not disclosed here. The amount cannot be added to Intel funding obligations without identifying overlap.

june_announcements.locator: June 15 release, Financial discipline and risk mitigation / Increased outlook; expands June 13 announcement
june_announcements.facts: EUR1.5–2.0B investment, supported and financed by long-term commitments from AMD and an unnamed technology customer, still subject to final negotiation/execution. Scope includes fitting out Plant2 and a new facility for substrate cores and advanced PCBs. Payments may contribute to current-year revenue and earnings; full operational impact follows over the next couple of years.
june_announcements.interpretation: This is not an immediate EUR1.5–2.0B production-capacity delivery or a disclosed wholly refundable prepaid-product balance. Current-year earnings include project economics; do not extrapolate those payments as perpetual substrate margin.

august_confirmation_and_conditions.locator: August 4 release, Expansion in Kulim and first-quarter cash-flow discussion; retrieved full HTML body
august_confirmation_and_conditions.facts: Expansion on schedule, but Kulim commitments remained subject to final negotiation and conclusion. June-quarter cash flow contained no significant inflows from the new Chongqing/Kulim customer agreements. Revenue and earnings contributions would be recognized over time with project progress and services. FY2026/27 capex remained EUR1.0–1.2B with positive operating FCF supported by expected customer payments.
august_confirmation_and_conditions.interpretation: Later than June, but not evidence that all funds had already arrived. Receipt and recognition differ. FY2026/27 refers to April 2026–March 2027, not calendar 2027.

september_named_customer_update.locator: Opening company announcement, second paragraph after the September 22 dateline; web full-body retrieval lines 210–213, exact sentence at 211; EQS News ID 2402726
september_named_customer_update.exact_primary_excerpt: Marvell Technology is the additional customer identified in AT&S’s previously announced expansion of its Kulim manufacturing site.
september_named_customer_update.retrieval: Primary issuer HTML full body successfully retrieved through web open, not merely a search snippet. Direct requests received403 and some other web opens timed out; the successful full-body retrieval supplied this sentence.
september_named_customer_update.facts: Announces a long-term agreement expanding advanced substrate capacity for Marvell, identifying it as the earlier unnamed customer. Reiterates Plant2 fit-out, new facility and long-term customer-supported investment.
september_named_customer_update.interpretation: This advances agreement status and conclusively resolves the June customer attribution. It does not disclose cash received, exact customer allocation, per-unit capacity, refresh economics or all final terms across the full investment program. Do not assign Marvell-supported capacity to Intel; possible indirect packaging relationships are not established here.

next_public_checkpoint.specific_test: Check actual customer receipts/contract liabilities, project revenue recognition, executed terms and revised Kulim commissioning dates. This is before the November 9 initial-screen deadline; it is not presently available evidence.

intel_forecast_implication.2027: No new quantified Intel substrate units from these announcements. Ibiden existing-plant support and late-FY2027 EMIB-T ramp keep some 2027 deliveries plausible; do not impose a blanket no-capacity claim.
intel_forecast_implication.2028: Existing EMIB-T plans support the feasibility of a larger packaging ramp, while supplier shortages and yield qualification still constrain its speed. The new JPY151B investment cannot be used to validate 2028 capacity. AT&S June expansion is not Intel-dedicated evidence.
intel_forecast_implication.cash_and_double_counting: Intel’s existing subsequent supply-agreement estimate is $5.3–6.1B, with about $3.3B expected paid by end 2027. Preserve the existing mapping among equipment, supplier advances, operating costs and supplier-capacity allowance. Supplier investment headlines are not automatically additional Intel commitments, additional capital spending, or customer grants received by Intel.
intel_forecast_implication.owned_judgment: Keep the existing funded phased ramp rather than raising 2027/2028 Intel capacity from these supplier headlines. The strongest concrete update removes an attribution error; it does not by itself prove a short or overturn the separately funded packaging opportunity.
intel_forecast_implication.limits: No issuer source here identifies Intel-specific good substrates, yields, package-qualified output or allocation shares. These missing quantities limit numeric transplantation, not the ability to make a prospective phased-ramp forecast.
